question: A single-celled fertilised egg is called a/an:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zygote.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zygote-**

 
 
• When a** female gamete (egg, or ovum) and a male gamete are combined, a zygote,** or fertilised egg cell, is produced (sperm).
 
• It contains all the **genetic information needed for a new organism to develop into a baby. **
 
• **In the brief zygote stage that follows cleavage, in which the single cell divides into smaller cells, in the embryonic development of humans and other animals, there are no more than a few cells in the zygote.​**
 
• The zygote can implant in the uterus, where it will develop into an embryo and fetus 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Embryo-**

 
 
• Embryo, the stage of an animal's early development while it is inside an egg or a mother's uterus.
 
• When referring to an unborn human, the phrase is used up to the end of the seventh week after conception; starting with the eighth week, the term "foetus" is used.
 
• It is the starting points in human growth.
 
 
 
• **blastocyte**
 
 
• **​**A blastocyst is a ball of cells that forms in the early stages of an embryo.
 
• It's a key stage in the development of a fetus and is especially important in in vitro fertilization (IVF). 
 
 
 
• **Foetus-**
 
 
• **​**A foetus is the stage of the embryo at which all of the bodily components are identifiable.
 
 

39:T
